editorial.headline: A Nationally Open Optical Trade That Bali Bars from PMA
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 46430 covers wholesale photographic and optical goods; national PMA openness is real, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks its PMA registration.
editorial.body:
For a foreign-owned company, KBLI 46430 cannot be registered for PMA in Bali today. That is the practical starting point, even though the activity is open to foreign investment nationally. The code covers the wholesale trade of photographic equipment and optical goods: the commercial supply of items such as spectacles, binoculars and magnifying glasses. It gives wholesale distributors a defined place when their business is trading these goods in volume.

The scale invitation is broad. The record opens the activity to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises—Micro, Small, Medium and Large in plain English. This is not a category limited to one size of operator; its reach spans the listed business scales. The important distinction is the character of the work itself: wholesale trade in the specified photographic and optical goods. That specificity matters because the code describes a particular commercial activity, not a loose retail or services label.

At national level, the PMA status is TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. Put plainly, the national setting allows full foreign ownership for this activity. The record traces that position to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. It is a clear national answer, and it is commercially meaningful—but it is not the final answer for a company seeking to register its PMA presence in Bali.

In Bali, the status is BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO. At the Besar scale, the OSS risk is Low or Medium-Low across every scope of this activity. Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium blocks PMA registration for activities in those risk bands; for this code, the record identifies the May 13, 2026 moratorium as the blocker. The divergence is structural rather than numerical: Bali does not set a lower foreign-equity ceiling or add a local condition. It blocks PMA registration. A founder can therefore hold both truths at once: nationally the activity is open to 100% foreign ownership, while in Bali it is unavailable for PMA registration.
editorial.pullQuote: This activity can be nationally open to 100% foreign ownership and still be unavailable for PMA registration in Bali.
